headline: EQUINOX-ORLA MERGER APPROVED BY SHAREHOLDERS — 99.91% Orla Vote; Court Hears July 28, Deal Closes July 31
snippet: Orla Mining shareholders approved the all-share business combination with Equinox Gold by 99.91% of votes cast at a special meeting held July 22, 2026, with Equinox Gold shareholders also approving their corresponding share issuance resolution at the same date; the combined entity will unite Orla's Camino Rojo mine in Mexico with Equinox's Nevada and Brazil assets into a significant multi-asset mid-tier producer. Orla will now seek a final order from the British Columbia Supreme Court at a hearing expected July 28, with the arrangement expected to close on or about July 31, 2026, pending applicable regulatory approvals that have already been received in Canada and Mexico.

headline: SILVER TESTS $61 ON SOFTENING JOBS DATA — Fourth Straight ADP Slowdown Unwinds Rate-Hike Bets; Gold at $4,155 Pre-FOMC
snippet: Gold climbed to $4,155 per ounce and silver pushed through the $61 level on July 23 as US ADP private-sector hiring data showed a fourth consecutive weekly slowdown — averaging 16,500 jobs per week over the four weeks ended July 4, down from 19,250 the prior period — reinforcing market expectations that the Federal Reserve will hold rates at the July 28–29 FOMC meeting and potentially signal a softer path ahead. Silver's run extends a five-day rally from the $57 range to its highest level in over a month, drawing energy from both fading rate-hike bets and the sixth consecutive annual supply deficit of 46.3 million ounces confirmed by the Silver Institute.

headline: NEW FOUND GOLD 43.52 g/t Au UNDERGROUND AT LOTTO — 23.66 g/t Channel Confirms Queensway Grade; 90,000m Program (NFG)
snippet: New Found Gold Corp. (TSX-V: NFG) released Phase 2 open pit and underground infill results from the Lotto Zone at its Queensway Gold Project in Newfoundland on July 21, 2026, with underground hole NFGC-25-2661 returning 43.52 g/t gold over 4.75 metres and channel sampling across the 210 by 70 metre Lotto excavation area returning 23.66 g/t Au over 15.88 metres (including 164.7 g/t Au over 2.11m) and 22.3 g/t Au over 3.60 metres, confirming that the grade block model is accurate and supports open-pit and underground resource definition. The Lotto Zone results are part of NFG's 90,000-metre 2026 drill program and confirm a shallow, high-grade gold system capable of supporting both bulk mining and selective high-grade underground scenarios.

headline: QMINES OPENS 10,000m CAMPAIGN WITH 18m AT 2.7 g/t Au, 1.7% Cu — Mt Chalmers Queensland 3-Rig DFS Push (ASX: QML)
snippet: QMines Limited (ASX: QML) announced July 22 that its 10,000-metre multi-rig drilling campaign — the largest program ever conducted at the Mt Chalmers copper-gold project 20 km northeast of Rockhampton, Queensland — is underway with the opening hole MCDD003 returning 18 metres at 2.7 g/t gold and 1.7% copper from 54 metres depth, including a high-grade 12-metre interval at 3.8 g/t Au and 2.0% Cu. The program is bifurcated into a 7,000-metre resource and DFS-support campaign targeting the Woods Shaft deposit and a 3,000-metre discovery campaign, with three rigs operating and assays pending from multiple completed holes, representing a material acceleration toward a Definitive Feasibility Study for the high-grade gold-copper-silver-zinc system.

headline: COPPER AT $6.48/LB, 5-WEEK HIGH — China $100/t Premium Spurs Refined Imports; Physical Market Tightest Since May 2025
snippet: Copper surged nearly 3% to $6.48 per pound on July 21 — a five-week high — as tightening physical market conditions in China pushed the country's import premium to $100 per tonne, the highest level since May 2025, after Beijing's crackdown on VAT fraud constrained scrap copper availability and forced manufacturers to switch to refined imports. The physical tightening arrived simultaneously with supply disruptions in Latin America, where Codelco halted surface operations at Andina and reported snowfall impacts at El Teniente, while multiple forecasters including the ICSG have flagged increasing deficit risk for 2026 as Chilean and Peruvian output constraints compound the scrap squeeze.

headline: KAZATOMPROM CUTS 10% AS URANIUM HOLDS $85.70 — Voluntary Discipline Floors Spot; NexGen Rook I Construction Underway
snippet: Uranium spot prices held near $85.70 per pound in late July — up 20% year-over-year and trading in a narrow range since April — anchored by Kazatomprom's intentional 10% reduction to its 2026 production guidance, a deliberate market-management action analysts compare to a 'nuclear OPEC' strategy that has established a price floor even as NexGen Energy broke ground on the 30-million-pound-per-year Rook I project in Saskatchewan following CNSC approval in March 2026. Cameco, meanwhile, has secured contracts for 230 million pounds of uranium through 2030, providing exceptional earnings visibility, while Denison Mines has completed its SaskPower 138kV transmission line connection at the Phoenix ISR mine site, keeping both projects on parallel development tracks with uranium's long-term demand fundamentals intact.

headline: ALL 27 RARE EARTHS UP IN JULY — Germanium +27.8%, Dysprosium +25.4% Lead; $151.7B Sector at New 2026 Highs
snippet: Every one of the 27 tracked rare earth elements rose in July 2026, marking a rare broad-based sector advance led by germanium at +27.8% month-over-month and dysprosium at +25.4% — both reaching new 2026 highs — while the combined market capitalization of 27 listed rare earth companies reached $151.7 billion with 10 companies in active production. The broad advance reflects a second consecutive year of structural supply deficits across most elements, tightening Chinese export controls and quota enforcement, and rising institutional attention driven by US military actions in Venezuela and renewed interest in Greenland's rare earth deposits that are accelerating Western-supply-chain investment.

headline: GOLD BULL VS BEAR JULY 2026: FOMC IS THE BINARY EVENT — $4,750 If Warsh Signals Pivot, $3,800 If He Stays Hawkish
snippet: Canadian Mining Report lays out two sharply divergent post-FOMC scenarios for gold: the bull case targets $4,750 per ounce in August if Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's July 29 statement signals that the tightening cycle is over or that rate cuts are on the table — arguing that the dovish language alone, even without a rate move, would push real yields lower and catalyze a wave of institutional buying into gold's record-setting bull run. The bear case targets $3,800 if Warsh delivers hawkish forward guidance or explicitly rules out cuts in 2026, noting that gold has corrected 10-25% on each of the last three hawkish Fed surprises and that a $4,000 close below support would likely trigger algorithmic momentum selling across gold miners and ETFs.

headline: 10 EVENTS TO WATCH THIS WEEK FOR GOLD AND SILVER — Flash PMI Friday, FOMC + Kinross Q2 + Agnico Q2 All Land July 29
snippet: International Stacker's weekly precious metals guide flags an unusually dense calendar for the week of July 20–26 and into the following week, with Friday July 25 Flash Manufacturing and Services PMI data serving as the final pre-FOMC macro signal before the July 28–29 Federal Open Market Committee decision — where a hold at 3.50–3.75% is priced at 85.6% odds but Kevin Warsh's post-meeting language is seen as the real market mover for gold, silver, and mining stocks. The July 29 convergence is particularly notable: Kinross Gold and Agnico Eagle Mines are both scheduled to release Q2 2026 production results after market close on the same day as the FOMC rate decision, creating simultaneous macro and fundamental catalysts that could produce outsized volatility in gold equities in either direction.

headline: SUMITOMO JOINS TINTINA MINES C$91M DEAL — July 23 Update on Domeyko Sulfuros Chile Copper Project (TSX-V: TTS)
snippet: Tintina Mines Limited (TSX-V: TTS) released a July 23 update to its landmark June 2, 2026 announcement of a C$91 million private placement and strategic partnership with Japan's Sumitomo Corporation and the Gignac family for the development of the Domeyko Sulfuros Copper-Gold Project in Chile's Atacama Region — a transaction that brings together one of Japan's leading trading houses with an experienced Canadian mining family to advance the project from exploration to Final Investment Decision. The offering is split into two tranches totalling C$91 million (with a further C$82 million in potential warrant proceeds) and consolidates 100% ownership of the Domeyko project, giving Sumitomo its first direct copper exposure in the prolific Atacama copper belt at a pre-production entry point.
